## Brand Strategy
- **Brand purpose:** "We believe movement inspires ideas. That is why we at Kia create the space for you to get inspired, and more time to bring your ideas to life."
- **Slogan:** "Movement that inspires."
- **What/How:** Design bold, original, inventive products; create user ownership and experiences that are simple, intuitive, and integrated.
- **Target:** Every modern individual who pursues their personal passion in this complex modern society.
- **Brand aspiration:** Mobility service provider beyond physical mobility -- pioneering and expanding new domains.

## Logo
- **Logo philosophy:** Three design concepts -- Symmetry (customer satisfaction, confidence), Rhythm (ceaseless change, moments of inspiration), Rising (absorbing customer perspective).
- **Construction:** Logotype form with 31-degree rising diagonal strokes. Beveled stroke ends reinforcing rising/aspiring character. Narrow connections between characters for continuous movement.
- **Anatomy:** Four key features -- beveled ends, modulated stroke widths, smooth precise curves with large interior spaces, narrow inter-character connections.
- **Clear space:** Defined by height unit (B). No other graphic elements permitted within clear space.
- **Minimum size:** Print 5mm / Digital 15px.
- **Logo colors:** Kia Midnight Black (PMS 7547 C / HEX #05141F) or Kia Polar White (#FFFFFF). Metallics (Gold PMS 871 C, Silver PMS 877 C) for special emphasis.
- **Background rules:** Grayscale guide (10%-100%) for choosing black or white logo.
- **Logo expansion:** Systematic lock-up rules for service/location names using Kia Signature Bold. Cap height matching, 3/4K spacing, horizontal and vertical combinations.
- **Co-branding:** Detailed height proportions (MAX 2K horizontal, MAX 3K vertical) with divider stroke (1/30 K).
- **Hyundai + Kia composition:** Specific dual-brand lock-up with proportional and color guidelines.
- **12 documented misuse rules** including no non-standard colors, no outlines, no low-res, no cropping, no skewing, no complex backgrounds, no rotation (except watermark patterns), no vertical usage.

## Typography
- **Corporate typeface:** Kia Signature -- custom bespoke typeface in Bold, Regular, Light.
  - Sharp edges with thickness for mechanical character; flowing strokes for human element.
  - Tall x-height for mobile screens and applications.
  - Vertical stroke ends connecting to logo aesthetic.
  - Latin, Greek, Coptic, Cyrillic, and Korean support.
- **Hierarchy (ratio-based):** H 100% (headline), H 60% (sub-headline), H 50-25% (body), H 20-15% (caption).
- **Latin specifications:** Headline Bold/Light, leading 100%; Sub-head Regular/Light, leading 125%; Body Light/Regular, leading 140%; Caption Regular/Bold, leading 140%.
- **Korean specifications:** Different leading values (130% headline, 150% sub-head, 160% body/caption). Optical kerning.
- **Notation rules:** "Kia" not "KIA" -- only K capitalized. Full name: Kia Corporation.

## Color
- **Color system (three-part):**
  1. **Primary (Opposites United):** Kia Midnight Black (PMS 7547 C / #05141F) + Kia Polar White (#FFFFFF)
  2. **Point color (Kianess/Automotive):** Kia Live Red -- symbolizes new ideas and dynamic energy. Heritage/culture color. Excluded from logos and motifs; used as accent in communications.
  3. **Secondary (Modern Individual's Lifestyle):**
     - Kia Afternoon Yellow: PMS P 7406 C / #F3C300
     - Kia Forest Green: PMS P 2279 C / #5D7D2B
     - Kia City Gray: PMS P 422 C / #9EA1A2
- **Color philosophy:** Primary black/white for perfection and harmony. Red for heritage recognition. Secondary colors for sustainability, eco-friendliness, smart mobility.
- **Usage hierarchy:** Primary (Midnight Black, Polar White) and Gray as main; Live Red as point; Secondary only when additional colors needed (graphs, diagrams).
- **Pantone, CMYK, RGB, and HEX** values provided for all colors.

## Graphics
- **Graphic motif system:** Three types derived from the logo's visual elements:
  - Type A: Placed on left side of material (5-10% margin); height 30-50% (vertical) or 30-80% (horizontal).
  - Type B: Adjusted to top 30-50% (vertical) or 50-70% (horizontal); horizontal line expanded 60-80% of width.
  - Type C: Horizontal materials only; diagonal line up to 40% height; minimum 10% right space; rounded corners (R = 0.1X).
- **Motif rules:** Must not appear to descend downwards. No purely straight horizontal/vertical lines. Anchor points within 2/3A to A range.
- **Thickness scaling:** 0.5pt (up to A6), 0.75pt (A6-A4), 1pt (A4-A3).
- **Logotype + motif placement:** Logo at left end of motif; distance > 1X; max logo size 50% of material width (Type A/B) or 30% of height (Type C).

## Photography
- Not documented as a separate section in the Basic System. Covered in the Application System (pages 57-123) and separate communication style guidelines.

## Applications
- Extensive Application System documented (pages 57-123) including vehicle applications, dealership/showroom, corporate communications. Referenced as separate chapters in a communication style guideline.
- **Pictograms:** 25 pictograms (direction, toilet, elevator, exit, smoking, parking, wheelchair, etc.) with diagonal/curved visual language derived from logo.
- **Icons:** 25 UI icons (navigation, lock/unlock, search, settings, play/pause, SNS, eco, fingerprint, etc.) matching Kia Signature typeface characteristics. Different weights available.

## Tone of Voice
- Not documented in this CI guideline. Separate brand communication materials likely exist.

## Outliers
- Ratio-based typography system (H 100%, H 60%, H 50%, H 20%) rather than fixed point sizes -- highly adaptable across scales.
- Three graphic motif types with precise mathematical placement rules (percentage margins, anchor point ranges, radius equations) -- extremely prescriptive.
- Korean and Latin typography treated as parallel systems with matched density and harmonized features -- demonstrating dual-script design thinking.
- Logo "rising" direction philosophy extends into motif rules (must not descend) -- consistent directional energy throughout the system.
- Hyundai + Kia composition rules formalize the parent/sibling brand relationship.
- Notation rule strictly prohibiting "KIA" (all caps) reflects the rebrand from the previous identity.
- Comprehensive pictogram and icon sets designed to visually echo the logo's curved, diagonal aesthetic.

## Quality Score
**5 / 5** -- Exhaustive corporate identity manual from a global automotive brand rebrand. Every element is meticulously specified with mathematical precision: logo construction angles (31 degrees, 45 degrees, 33 degrees), motif placement percentages, ratio-based typography, and detailed co-branding frameworks. The dual Latin/Korean typography system is a standout. The graphic motif system offers remarkable depth for consistent yet flexible application. Only missing dedicated photography and tone of voice sections (likely in separate guidelines).
